canvas.title: Attention Is All You Need — Reasoning Map

nodes.body_md:
# Introduction

## Can sequence transduction drop recurrence entirely?

# Background

## Why prior parallel alternatives still struggle with long range?

## Sequential RNN bottleneck

### Recurrent models block within-example parallelization because each hidden state depends on the previous step.
- LSTM and gated RNNs were the prior default for language modeling and translation.
- Attention already modeled distance-independent dependencies, but almost always with an RNN.

# Model Architecture

## How is an encoder–decoder built from attention alone?

## CNN path-length limits

### Convolutional alternatives parallelize over positions, but relating distant tokens still grows with distance.
- Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet, and ConvS2S compute all positions in parallel.
- Relating two positions costs O(n) for ConvS2S and O(log n) for ByteNet; the Transformer reduces that to a constant, offsetting averaging loss with Multi-Head Attention.

## Propose the Transformer

### The Transformer draws global input–output dependencies with attention alone, enabling far more parallel training.
- It dispenses with recurrence and convolutions.
- The authors report a new translation SOTA after as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

# Why Self-Attention

## Why prefer self-attention over recurrence or convolution?

## Sinusoidal positional encoding

### Without recurrence or convolution, order is injected by fixed sinusoidal positional encodings added to embeddings.
- PE uses sine/cosine at geometric wavelengths so relative offsets are linear in PE space.
- Learned positional embeddings matched quality; sinusoids were kept for possible length extrapolation.

## First fully self-attentive model

### To the authors' knowledge, the Transformer is the first transduction model that relies entirely on self-attention without sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.

# Training

## What regime makes the architecture trainable at scale?

# Results

## Do quality and speed gains hold beyond the design arguments?

## Data, schedule, regularization

### Models train on WMT 2014 En–De (~4.5M pairs) and En–Fr (36M sentences) with Adam warmup and residual dropout plus label smoothing.
- Batches hold ~25K source and 25K target tokens on 8 P100 GPUs.
- Base: 100K steps (~12 h); big: 300K steps (3.5 days).

# Conclusion

## What does the paper claim, and what remains open?

## Open directions

### The authors leave non-text modalities, restricted local attention for very long inputs, and less sequential generation as future work.
- They also note restricted neighborhoods as a planned path for long sequences earlier in the complexity discussion.

## Attention-only transduction

### The Transformer is presented as the first sequence transduction model based entirely on multi-headed self-attention.
- It trains substantially faster than recurrent or convolutional encoder–decoders.
- It sets a new state of the art on both WMT 2014 translation tasks reported here.

## Stacked encoder–decoder

### Both stacks use N=6 layers of multi-head attention and position-wise FFNs with residuals and LayerNorm.
- Encoder: self-attention then FFN; all widths use d_model=512.
- Decoder adds encoder–decoder attention and masks future positions to keep auto-regression.

![Source figure](attention-c142ca02f15e03.webp)

## Constant path length

### Self-attention connects all positions with O(1) sequential operations and short maximum path length.
- Recurrent layers need O(n) sequential steps; convolutions need stacked layers to cover long range.
- When sequence length n is smaller than width d—as in typical MT sentence encodings—self-attention is also computationally favorable.

![Source figure](attention-81c8970cb2e2e8.webp)

## Scaled multi-head attention

### Scaled Dot-Product Attention with h=8 heads is the core compute primitive.
- Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V; scaling stabilizes large d_k.
- Heads use d_k=d_v=64; the same block serves encoder self-attention, masked decoder self-attention, and encoder–decoder attention.

![Source figure](attention-ff3f05521b1d97.webp)

## Translation SOTA

### Transformer (big) reaches BLEU 28.4 on WMT 2014 En→De and 41.0 on En→Fr at a fraction of prior training cost.
- En→De improves over previous best models, including ensembles, by more than 2 BLEU.
- Even the base model beats prior published models and ensembles.

![Source figure](attention-c680fb3d6ace3d.webp)

## Ablations and parsing

### Component ablations and constituency parsing support the design and show task transfer.
- Single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse; shrinking d_k hurts; larger models and dropout help; learned PE ≈ sinusoidal.
- A lightly tuned 4-layer Transformer beats BerkeleyParser on WSJ-only data and trails only RNNG among reported systems.

![Source figure](attention-9af6d1f9ded531.webp)
